goal: Repair the staff sign-in policy while keeping legitimate staff access available.
context: Builds on the distinction between verifying identity and deciding what an identity may access. All password properties and proof results are supplied.

concepts.title: Check a proposed password
concepts.text: A minimum length sets the shortest acceptable password. A separate list blocks common or compromised passwords. An entry can meet the length requirement and still be on the list. Evaluate the proposal when setting or changing the password.

concepts.title: Respond to a compromise report
concepts.text: Knowing the existing password can still produce a match after it has been exposed. When a compromise is confirmed, require an approved replacement before allowing normal sign-in.

concepts.title: Require a different kind of proof
concepts.text: A password and a memorized code are both things a person knows. A device can prove that it holds a private key. A public certificate can help identify that key; presenting the certificate alone proves no possession. A local biometric can unlock the bound device, which then supplies the key proof. Some systems use a device-based authenticator instead of a password. This activity keeps the password and adds a second factor.

worked.label: Check the password proposal
worked.value:
18 characters · long enough
Listed as compromised · deny
worked.explanation: Length and list membership answer different questions. A long password can still be listed.

worked.label: Follow a compromise report
worked.value:
Old password matches
Compromise confirmed → replace first
worked.explanation: Require replacement because the previously accepted password is no longer trustworthy.

worked.label: Compare proof of identity
worked.value:
Password + memorized code · knowledge only
Password + device key proof · knowledge and possession
worked.explanation: The key proof adds a different factor. The device still needs to demonstrate possession even when unlocked locally with a biometric.

practice.title: Repair the password proposal checks
practice.action: In Minimum length, enter 15. Turn on Reject listed passwords.
practice.observe: The short proposal and the longer listed proposal are denied. The new staff phrase is accepted.

practice.title: Pick the second proof
practice.action: Set Additional proof to Bound authenticator.
practice.observe: Compare the certificate-only and the certificate-with-key trials. The biometric trial works when the device supplies key proof.

practice.title: Handle the reported compromise
practice.action: Turn on Require replacement after compromise, then select Check workspace. Try a higher minimum and notice when the approved staff phrase stops passing.
practice.observe: The confirmed compromise now needs replacement. A threshold that is too high can reject an approved proposal.

requirements: Reject the short and listed proposals. Keep the supplied new staff phrase eligible.
Require a replacement after confirmed compromise.
Require the valid password and bound authenticator proof. Accept both supported device proof methods and reject the incomplete sign-in trials.

review.introduction: Teaches the relevant decisions with separate worked values and plain-language explanations.
review.example: Connects guided changes beside the actual controls to current trials and observes exclusions.
review.assignment: Checks virtual policy behavior with supplied outcomes and reports individual failures.

goal: Repair the virtual VPN policies for a branch LAN and an individual remote device.
context: Builds on IPv4 prefixes and routed traffic paths. An IPsec tunnel policy relates the outer devices on the path to the inner addresses whose traffic is selected for protection.

concepts.title: Start with the participants
concepts.text: A site-to-site design joins two networks through their security gateways. Remote access connects one remote device to an office gateway. Use the role of each participant to decide which device handles the tunnel.

concepts.title: Separate the two sets of addresses
concepts.text: The outer addresses identify the tunnel endpoints. The inner addresses identify the original source and destination. A gateway can protect an entire LAN. One remote client can have a single assigned inner address, written as a /32 prefix.

concepts.title: Limit protection to the intended traffic
concepts.text: Match the prefixes on both sides. A remote device may need only one office service range. Use a trial just beyond that range and a normal same-LAN trial to verify the policy leaves those paths alone.

worked.label: Join two sites
worked.explanation: Use the branch and office gateways. The selected inner ranges cover both networks.

worked.label: Connect the remote device
worked.explanation: Use the remote device and office gateway. The rest of the office LAN is outside this remote profile.

worked.label: Read a path trial
worked.value:
Inner destination 10.50.20.95 · selected
Inner destination 10.50.20.96 · outside
worked.explanation: The service range ends at .95. These are policy address comparisons; the trial does not treat the range endpoints as host assignments.

practice.title: Repair the branch profile
practice.action: In the site-to-site profile select the branch and office gateways. Set their respective inner ranges to 10.40.10.0/24 and 10.40.20.0/24.
practice.observe: The two branch/office directions need the same protected relationship. A /25 misses the second branch host.

practice.title: Limit the remote profile
practice.action: Use the remote device and office gateway. Keep the device’s assigned address as a /32, and narrow the office side to 10.40.20.0/27. Select Apply profiles.
practice.observe: The supplied allowed service uses the remote profile. The adjacent service is outside its protected traffic.

practice.title: Check which paths change
practice.action: Select Check workspace. Compare the outer endpoint addresses for the office paths and the ordinary branch LAN trial. Change one prefix and apply again.
practice.observe: Only applied changes affect the path trials. Traffic within one LAN stays local.

requirements: Protect exchanges between the full branch and office LANs with the two gateways.
Protect the individual remote device’s traffic to the listed office service range only.
Apply both profiles and verify the reverse direction, the adjacent excluded service, and ordinary same-LAN traffic.
